title: Document Similarity & Plagiarism Detection
short_description: Learn how educational and publishing systems compare documents, detect common content, identify suspicious patterns, and analyze repeated text efficiently.

real_world_context.problem: Educational and publishing systems need to compare documents to identify common content, measure textual differences, locate suspicious patterns, and detect repeated or duplicated sections.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Efficient string and dynamic programming algorithms allow document-analysis systems to process large amounts of text and identify similarities or differences effectively.

learning_objectives: Understand how document content can be represented using strings.
Apply Dynamic Programming to find the Longest Common Subsequence between two documents.
Apply Edit Distance to measure the minimum changes required between two documents.
Use KMP Pattern Matching to efficiently locate suspicious patterns in large documents.
Apply matching-window techniques to identify the longest continuous section shared by two documents.
Analyze repeated substrings to detect duplicated content within a document.
Choose an appropriate algorithm based on document size and the type of similarity being measured.

real_world_mapping.document_content: String representing the contents of a document
real_world_mapping.common_sequence: Content appearing in both documents in the same order
real_world_mapping.edit_distance: Minimum number of changes required between two documents
real_world_mapping.text_pattern: Suspicious phrase or sequence being searched for
real_world_mapping.pattern_occurrence: Location where a suspicious pattern appears
real_world_mapping.matching_window: Continuous text section shared by two documents
real_world_mapping.repeated_substring: Duplicated text appearing within the same document
real_world_mapping.similarity_analysis: Process of identifying common or duplicated content
real_world_mapping.plagiarism_detection: Identification of potentially copied or reused text

completion_message: You have completed the Document Similarity & Plagiarism Detection scenario. You have learned how dynamic programming, pattern matching, matching-window techniques, and substring analysis can be applied to document comparison and plagiarism detection.
